Incorporating Beige Book insights alongside the July 29, 2020 FOMC decision:

- Policy stance: Highly accommodative at the ELB with continued Treasury/agency MBS/CMBS purchases, active repo and ON RRP facilities, all aimed at supporting market functioning and credit flow.
- Beige Book conditions: Activity improved modestly across most Districts as reopenings lifted consumer spending and vehicle sales; manufacturing and construction revived; residential real estate strengthened on low mortgage rates. Offsetting this, commercial real estate remained weak (particularly retail and hospitality), the energy sector was depressed, and uncertainty around the outlook stayed elevated. Prices were muted and employment gains were uneven, with significant slack.
- Credit: While market functioning improved, banks tightened lending standards and terms, keeping the bank-lending channel restrictive and tempering transmission to the real economy.
- Implication: The economy is stabilizing with notable rebounds in goods and housing, but services, energy, and CRE remain significant drags; risks remain skewed to the downside given virus-related uncertainty.

Adjusted tone vs. the SLOOS-only view: less negative given observed rebounds, but still cautious due to sectoral weakness and tight credit.
